# Output Contracts

Exact formats for everything `wb-paper-setup` writes, and the playback
protocol. These formats are contracts: `wb-paper-write` and `wb-paper-review`
parse these files, and users edit them by hand. Keep the section headings
exactly as specified; keep the content plain markdown.

## `wb-paper/profile.md`

```markdown
# Paper Profile
<!-- Generated by wb-paper-setup on <date>. Edit freely — your edits win. -->

## Paper facts
Working title, paper type (applied empirical / theory / mixed / descriptive),
method(s), data (source, unit, period), target outlet (for example a journal
or working-paper series), draft stage,
deadline/milestone, coauthors + voice agreement, formats in use.

## Grounding pointers
- Draft: <path or "none yet">
- Outputs (tables/figures): <path(s)>
- Bibliography: <path or "none">
Rules for consumers: wb-paper-write takes numbers ONLY from these outputs and
marks everything else [AUTHOR: ...]; wb-paper-review checks draft numbers
against these outputs.

## Positioning (human-authored)
The paper's intellectual core — direct human input per
shared/aitl-protocol.md § 5. Four elements, each in the author's confirmed
words:
- Main finding: <one sentence, magnitude if known>
- Contribution: <what is new> · Type(s), ranked: method / evidence / theory /
  practice / policy
- Relevance: <one sentence — who should care and why now>
- Claim sentence: "This paper is the first to / the best evidence that ..."
Record origin per element: (human verbatim) or (human seed + AI sharpening —
chose variant B with edits). Unsettled elements are recorded as unsettled:
"Not yet settled — candidate framings the author is weighing: ..." — guides
then make this a top priority, and wb-paper-write re-asks before drafting any
section that needs the element.

## Audience
Primary and secondary readers; what each needs to be convinced of.

## Feedback priorities
- Wants: <what the author asked feedback to focus on>
- Fears: <what the author most fears a smart reader would say>
- From past reviews: <recurring themes, if Protocol C ran>

## Voice fingerprint
(If Protocol B ran.) Rhythm, person/stance, hedging profile, signature moves
(protected), vocabulary temperature. Facts, not judgments.

## Conventions
Grouped by tag (structure / tone / results / tables / policy / method).
Deltas only — the vendored econ-write skill is the baseline and is never
restated here (see the delta rule in source-extraction.md). Each entry:
- **<short name>**: <operational rule, imperative>
  - Check: <one-pass verification a guide can run when commenting>
  - Evidence: <source>, "<fragment ≤ 25 words>" (<location>)
  - Applies to: <scope> · Tag: <tag>
Negative entries from anti-exemplars use the same shape ("Never ...").
Entries that conflict with baseline are marked `overrides baseline: <econ-write
section>`. Baseline rules the author especially cares about appear as guide
priorities (pointers), not as entries here.

## Non-negotiables
Verbatim list of things the AI must never change or flag. Consumers treat
these as hard scope guards.

## Outlet constraints
(If Protocol D ran.) Hard checkable constraints only, one per line, with
provenance. Include the target outlet's AI-use/disclosure policy verbatim if published.

## Provenance log
Inventory of wb-paper/references/ at setup time (per folder, per file, with
tags/dislikes/bindingness/fairness calls from interview Part R); what was
inspected (with dates), what was skipped or unreadable, which answers were
defaults, what was inferred vs. told, conflicts and how they were resolved,
untransferable candidates that were dropped.
```

Rules:

- Every claim in the profile traces to the interview, an extraction, or is
  marked `(default)` or `(inferred — confirmed at playback)`.
- The Provenance log makes the profile auditable — never omit it. It is also
  the teaching artifact: users should be able to see exactly how their answers
  became instructions.

## `wb-paper/guides/<name>.md`

One file per guide. Filename: kebab-case (`methods.md`, `policy.md`,
`writing.md`, `the-referee-you-keep-getting.md`). Format:

```markdown
# Guide: <Name>
<!-- Personalized by wb-paper-setup on <date>. Edit freely — this guide
     works for you, for drafting and for comments. -->

## What this guide is
One or two sentences a newcomer can understand. Not "I am a reviewer."

## When drafting
What the drafter must follow (order, claims, tone, what never to do).

## When commenting
What to check, and what to leave to other guides.

## Mandate
The same substance, in the guide's voice, 2–4 sentences.

## Scope guard
What this guide must NOT cover: territory owned by other guides, plus every
profile non-negotiable, plus voice-fingerprint features (for the Writing
guide: the fingerprint is style, not error).

## Priorities (ranked)
1. <top priority — from the author's fears / referee themes>
2. ...
Max 6. The review runs top-down; if the budget runs out, low priorities are
skipped, never the top ones.

## Baseline to enforce
Named sections of the vendored baseline skills this persona enforces (e.g.
"econ-write › Avoiding AI-Generated Writing Patterns", "upstream-econ-review ›
gates/did.md"). Pointers only — never copied text.

## Conventions to enforce
The subset of profile convention entries this persona owns, referenced by
short name (do not duplicate the entry text — the profile is the source of
truth). Entries marked `overrides baseline` outrank the Baseline list above.

## Severity calibration
How strict to be given the draft stage (from Paper facts). Concept-stage:
structural issues only, no polish comments. Submission-stage: everything.

## Comment format
Every comment: **Quote** the passage (or state the checked comparison) →
**Concern** (why it matters for THIS paper, referencing the contribution
claim or a convention) → **Suggestion** (concrete, proportionate) →
**Severity** (P0 blocks credibility / P1 weakens the paper / P2 polish).
Never edit the manuscript. Never rewrite passages unasked — suggest, don't
substitute.
```

Rules:

- Stock guides are copied from `SKILL_ROOT/guides/` and then personalized
  in Priorities, Conventions to enforce, Scope guard, and Severity
  calibration. Mandate and Comment format stay close to stock. Always fill
  **When drafting** and **When commenting**.
- Scope guards must be mutually consistent across the set: every convention
  is owned by exactly one guide; non-negotiables appear in every scope guard.

## Playback protocol (Stage 7 — mandatory, every route)

Before writing any file, show in chat:

1. **Paper digest** — 3–5 lines: what the paper is, where it's going, the
   contribution claim.
2. **Top conventions** — the 5 most consequential convention entries, each
   with its evidence fragment, so the user can spot a misreading instantly.
3. **Guides** — each guide: plain name, one line for drafting, one line for
   commenting, its #1 priority. Two candidate sets, as a choice.
4. **Flags** — everything inferred rather than told; every conflict and the
   proposed resolution; every opt-in question (recurring-weakness watch,
   bespoke guide offer).

Open the summary with "Nothing is saved yet." Ask for corrections first, as
its own turn. Apply them and re-show only what changed. The roster choice is
the next message, not a second questionnaire bolted onto the summary. Write
files only after an explicit go-ahead ("looks good", "go ahead", "write it").
"Ok", silence, or answering a different question is not a go-ahead. Say that
yourself; do not wait for the user to forbid writing. If they go quiet, leave
the summary in chat and stop.

After writing: list the files created, commit them yourself per the git
convention in `shared/aitl-protocol.md` (the skill commits its own actions;
only suggest `git init` when there is no repo), and state the two next moves —
"edit any file by hand" and, matching the choice they made at the start,
either start drafting or start comments.

## `wb-paper/outline.md` (written by wb-paper-write, outline mode)

```markdown
# Outline — <working title>
<!-- Chosen from variants A/B on <date>; see ledger. Edit freely. -->

## Writing order
1. <section> — <one-line rationale>   (e.g. Introduction first, Abstract last)
...

## Sections
### <Section name>   [status: not-started | ai-outline | ai-draft | human-edited]
- Job: <what this section must accomplish>
- Carries: <positioning element(s), or "—">
- Uses: <exhibits/outputs, or "—">
```

Section names here are the canonical section list for the ledger's status
table — keep them in sync. Draft-mode updates the per-section status lines.

## `wb-paper/log.md` — the ledger

Format, git commit convention, decision rule, human-touched reconciliation,
and disclosure generation are defined in `shared/aitl-protocol.md`. That
protocol is part of this contract: every skill that touches `wb-paper/` or
the manuscript writes ledger entries immediately after acting and commits per
the convention. `wb-paper-setup` initializes the ledger at Stage 0 (scaffold),
so entries can be written immediately from Stage 1 on.

## Consumer notes (for wb-paper-write / wb-paper-review authors)

- Parse by the exact `##` headings above; tolerate extra user-added sections
  and never remove them.
- User hand-edits are authoritative. If a consumer skill finds a profile
  instruction it cannot follow, it says so rather than silently ignoring it.
- `wb-paper-review` must present the guides and ask which to use for this
  pass (and in what order) on every invocation — using all guides is a user
  choice, never a default. When listing them, restate in one line what each
  guide checks, for someone who does not remember the setup.
- Both consumers follow `shared/aitl-protocol.md`: decision gates with ≥2
  options, ledger entries per action, one-AI-action-one-commit, human-touched
  reconciliation at run start, positioning elements never invented.
